verdict_reason: Re-deriving Rudman et al.'s construction gives IsoScore=(PR-1)/(d-1), exactly what _isoscore computes after zero-padding the covariance spectrum to ambient dimension. It reproduced the paper's rank-spectrum anchor to 5.55e-17 absolute and matched the authors' IsoScore 2.0.1 implementation on ordinary and rank-deficient clouds to at most 2.02e-8 absolute, with no formula counterexample.
comparable_reason: Raw IsoScore=(PR-1)/(d_model-1), so a fixed effective rank is mechanically divided by ambient width; in 66 models rho=-0.433 with d_model (p=2.84e-4) and -0.310 with n_layers (p=0.011). The explicit isoscore_effective_dims=IsoScore*(d-1)+1 recovers PR and is clean in the same table: rho=-0.089 with width (p=0.477), -0.039 with depth (p=0.756), and -0.031 with vocabulary (p=0.805).
github_reason: Fetched the authors' implementation and ran IsoScore 2.0.1 on identical ordinary, exact-rank, and N<d clouds. The metric kernel matched to at most about 2.02e-8 absolute in the fresh check, including official 0.1513987667 versus BLME 0.1513987869 on the 20x100 cloud; the separate public-task exclusion policy is recorded under defects rather than used to downgrade formula parity.
paper_reason: Rudman et al. Table 2 gives IsoScore(I_d^(k))=(k-1)/(d-1). For k=4,d=10 the published value is 1/3 and the current public task returned 0.33333333333333326 (absolute error 5.55e-17) when the same covariance spectrum was represented with 80 rows; isoscore_effective_dims returned 4.0.
confounds_reason: The raw score's exact denominator creates a width proxy, confirmed by rho=-0.433 with d_model and rho=-0.463 with parameter count in the 66-model sweep. The effective-dimension inversion removes those associations (all four width/depth/vocabulary/parameter correlations nonsignificant, |rho|<=0.142).
defects: CODE isotropy.py:249-253 NaN-gates every N<=d cloud although Algorithm 1 explicitly scores zero covariance eigenvalues and the official package scores these clouds; the measured 20x100 counterexample changes 0.15139877 to NaN.

CODE the cached route consumes all retained tokens while collect_hidden_states on the uncached single-layer route keeps at most ten tokens per document, so the same nominal task can score different populations and can cross the hard gate solely by execution route.

CONFIG documentation at defaults.yaml:18-25 still says the configured N/d>=50 threshold is enforced, but current code only records that flag and gates at N<=d; the effective behavior and prose disagree.

COMPARABILITY: raw IsoScore is exactly a normalized participation ratio and is not cross-width neutral; isoscore_effective_dims is the correct separately named inversion but duplicates geometry_svd.participation_ratio and must remain deduplicated downstream.
